task_instance: Set up a GitHub Actions CI quality-gate pipeline (.github/workflows/ci.yml) for a small sample Node/TypeScript project (sample-widget-app), covering lint, type check, unit tests, build, and security audit gates as parallel/dependent jobs, plus a Dependabot config, matching the scripts declared in the project's package.json.
evidence: Created package.json defining lint/typecheck/test/build/audit scripts, src/index.ts as a stand-in source file, .github/workflows/ci.yml with 5 jobs (lint, typecheck, test run in parallel; build needs all three; security-audit needs build), .github/dependabot.yml for weekly npm updates, and README.md documenting the setup and verification. Verified the deliverable by: (1) reading the written ci.yml back and manually checking indentation and key nesting (name/on/jobs -> job -> runs-on/steps/needs) matches the GitHub Actions schema shown in the skill document's example YAML; (2) confirming every 'run:' line in the workflow (npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm test, npm run build, npm run audit) corresponds exactly to a script defined in package.json, so the config is internally consistent with the target project; (3) confirming the pipeline's trigger block (pull_request/push to main) and job structure mirrors the skill's 'Basic CI Pipeline' and 'Example: caching and parallelism' sections. This is the skill's core stated deliverable ('Setting up a new project's CI pipeline') and is inherently a text-file artifact (YAML config), so it was fully producible and verifiable (by manual schema/consistency review) without code execution. Items requiring execution or GitHub account access -- actually running the workflow on a runner, configuring branch protection/required status checks, storing real GitHub Secrets, triggering a deployment -- were correctly identified as out of scope for this runtime and were not attempted (documented in README.md under 'Explicitly out of scope').
